questions.q: A manufacturer wants one integrated system where a purchase order automatically updates inventory and the general ledger. Which core idea of ERP does this illustrate?
opts: Separate best-of-breed applications per department linked by monthly file uploads
A spreadsheet-based consolidation performed at period end
A single integrated database shared by logistics and finance processes
An external data warehouse used only for reporting
questions.ex: ERP systems integrate business processes on a shared database, so a logistics transaction such as a goods receipt updates finance in real time.

questions.q: Which SAP module is primarily responsible for purchasing and inventory management?
opts: MM (Materials Management)
SD (Sales and Distribution)
CO (Controlling)
PP (Production Planning)
questions.ex: MM covers procurement, purchase orders, goods receipts and inventory; SD handles selling, CO internal cost accounting, and PP manufacturing.

questions.q: Which best describes what a capital markets platform such as Murex MX.3 or Calypso provides?
opts: Retail deposit and loan account servicing for branch customers
Payroll and HR processing for financial institutions
Card payment authorisation for merchants
Front-to-back trade capture, pricing, risk management, operations and accounting for traded products
questions.ex: MX.3 and Calypso are cross-asset platforms covering the trade lifecycle from front-office capture and valuation through risk, settlement processing and accounting.

questions.q: Which type of organisation is the most typical user of Murex MX.3 or Calypso?
opts: A small retail shop managing its stock
An investment or commercial bank trading derivatives and managing treasury
A hospital scheduling patient appointments
A logistics company tracking shipments
questions.ex: These platforms are used mainly by banks, and also by asset managers, insurers and large corporate treasuries, to trade and manage financial instruments.

questions.q: In standard SAP procure-to-pay, what is the correct sequence of documents?
opts: Purchase order → purchase requisition → invoice → goods receipt → payment
Purchase requisition → goods receipt → purchase order → payment → invoice
Purchase requisition → purchase order → goods receipt → invoice receipt → payment
Invoice receipt → purchase order → goods receipt → payment → purchase requisition
questions.ex: A requisition expresses the internal need, the PO commits to the vendor, the goods receipt records delivery, the invoice is verified, and finally the vendor is paid.

questions.q: A company pays a vendor invoice of 5,000 that was previously posted. What is the journal entry for the outgoing payment?
opts: Debit Bank 5,000; Credit Vendor 5,000
Debit Inventory 5,000; Credit Bank 5,000
Debit GR/IR 5,000; Credit Bank 5,000
Debit Vendor (accounts payable) 5,000; Credit Bank 5,000
questions.ex: Paying the vendor clears the payable, so accounts payable is debited and cash in the bank is credited.

questions.q: In a bank's trade lifecycle, which function typically handles trade confirmations and settlement?
opts: Back office
Front office
Middle office
Sales coverage
questions.ex: The back office performs post-trade operations such as confirmation matching, settlement and payments.

questions.q: Which activity is most characteristic of the middle office?
opts: Negotiating prices with clients and booking trades
Sending SWIFT payment instructions to counterparties
Independent risk measurement, limit monitoring and daily P&L control
Designing the bank's marketing campaigns
questions.ex: The middle office independently monitors risk and limits, validates valuations and controls P&L, separate from the front office that executes trades.

questions.q: A goods receipt of 2,000 is posted for a PO, but the vendor invoice has not yet arrived. What is the balance on the GR/IR clearing account for this PO?
opts: Zero, because GR/IR only updates at payment
2,000 debit
2,000 credit
4,000 credit
questions.ex: The goods receipt posts Debit Inventory, Credit GR/IR, leaving a 2,000 credit until the invoice posts Debit GR/IR, Credit Vendor and clears it.

questions.q: What does the three-way match in invoice verification compare?
opts: The purchase order, the goods receipt and the vendor invoice
The sales order, the delivery and the billing document
The bank statement, the general ledger and the payment run
The purchase requisition, the vendor master and the payment terms
questions.ex: Three-way match checks that quantities and prices agree across the PO, what was actually received, and what the vendor invoiced before payment.

questions.q: What is a key difference between a futures contract and a forward contract?
opts: Forwards are exchange-traded while futures are traded over the counter
Futures are standardised, exchange-traded and settled daily through margin, while forwards are private OTC agreements
Futures have no counterparty obligation to transact
Forwards can only be written on commodities
questions.ex: Futures trade on exchanges with standard terms, a clearing house and daily mark-to-market, whereas forwards are customised bilateral OTC contracts usually settled at maturity.

questions.q: A non-dividend-paying stock trades at 100. The risk-free rate is 5% per annum with continuous compounding. What is the 1-year forward price (to two decimals)?
questions.ex: F = S·e^(rT) = 100 × e^0.05 = 105.13; 105.00 would be simple interest, not continuous compounding.

questions.q: In SAP order-to-cash, what is the correct sequence?
opts: Billing → sales order → delivery → incoming payment
Sales order → delivery (with goods issue) → billing → incoming payment
Delivery → sales order → incoming payment → billing
Sales order → billing → incoming payment → delivery
questions.ex: The sales order captures the demand, the delivery and post goods issue ship the goods, billing creates the invoice, and the customer payment clears the receivable.

questions.q: When post goods issue is performed for a delivery with an inventory cost of 600, which journal entry is created?
opts: Debit Customer 600; Credit Revenue 600
Debit Inventory 600; Credit Cost of goods sold 600
Debit Bank 600; Credit Customer 600
Debit Cost of goods sold 600; Credit Inventory 600
questions.ex: Goods issue reduces stock at cost, so cost of goods sold is debited and inventory is credited; revenue is posted later at billing.

questions.q: For most major currency pairs, when does a standard FX spot trade settle?
opts: Two business days after the trade date (T+2)
On the trade date (T+0)
One week after the trade date
At the end of the calendar month
questions.ex: Spot FX conventionally settles T+2 for most pairs, with a few exceptions such as USD/CAD at T+1.

questions.q: EUR/USD spot is 1.1000 (USD per EUR). The 1-year USD rate is 5% and the 1-year EUR rate is 3%, both simple annual. Under covered interest parity, what is the 1-year forward rate (to four decimals)?
questions.ex: F = 1.1000 × (1.05 / 1.03) = 1.1214; the lower-yielding EUR trades at a forward premium against USD.

questions.q: A customer order exceeds the customer's credit limit and automatic credit checking is active. What is the typical system outcome?
opts: The order is blocked for credit review and cannot proceed to delivery until released
The credit limit is automatically increased to fit the order
The order is converted into a purchase order
The order is posted directly to the general ledger as bad debt
questions.ex: Credit management checks the exposure against the limit and places the document on a credit block until an authorised person releases it.

questions.q: Under IFRS 15 / ASC 606, when is revenue recognised?
opts: When the sales order is entered
When cash is received from the customer, in all cases
When (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control of goods or services
At the end of the fiscal year regardless of delivery
questions.ex: The five-step model recognises revenue when control passes to the customer, which is not necessarily when the order is taken or cash is collected.

questions.q: A rate is 10% per annum with continuous compounding. What is the equivalent rate with annual compounding (to two decimals)?
questions.ex: Equivalent annual rate = e^0.10 − 1 = 10.52%; 9.53% is ln(1.10), the reverse conversion.

questions.q: The 1-year zero rate is 4% and the 2-year zero rate is 5%, both continuously compounded. What is the forward rate for the period from year 1 to year 2?
At month end, a company has received consulting services worth 3,000 but no invoice has arrived. Which accrual entry is posted in the close?
opts: Debit Accrued liabilities 3,000; Credit Consulting expense 3,000
Debit Vendor 3,000; Credit Bank 3,000
Debit Prepaid expenses 3,000; Credit Bank 3,000
Debit Consulting expense 3,000; Credit Accrued liabilities 3,000
questions.ex: Accrual accounting records the expense in the period it is incurred, with an accrued liability until the invoice is received.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a bank reconciliation in the record-to-report process?
opts: To explain and resolve differences between the bank statement and the bank account in the general ledger
To set credit limits for customers
To calculate depreciation on fixed assets
To release purchase orders for payment
questions.ex: Bank reconciliation matches ledger cash to the bank statement and identifies items such as outstanding payments or unrecorded fees before the books are closed.

questions.q: Market yields on a fixed-coupon bond rise. What happens to the bond's price?
opts: It rises
It falls
It stays the same because the coupon is fixed
It always moves to par
questions.ex: A bond's price is the present value of fixed cash flows, so a higher discount rate gives a lower price.

questions.q: A bond has a modified duration of 6. If its yield rises by 50 basis points, what is the approximate percentage change in its price?
opts: About −3.0%
About +3.0%
About −0.3%
About −6.0%

questions.q: In SAP FI, which standard posting keys are typically used for a debit and a credit to a G/L account?
opts: 01 debit, 11 credit
31 debit, 21 credit
40 debit, 50 credit
50 debit, 40 credit
questions.ex: Posting key 40 is a G/L debit and 50 a G/L credit; 01/11 are customer keys and 21/31 are vendor keys.

questions.q: Which standard SAP document type is commonly used for a customer payment?
opts: KR
SA
DR
DZ
questions.ex: DZ is the customer payment document type; DR is a customer invoice, KR a vendor invoice and SA a G/L account document.

questions.q: Table orders has columns id, customer, amount. Which query returns the three largest orders, largest first?
opts: SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY amount ASC LIMIT 3;
SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY amount DESC LIMIT 3;
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount > 3 ORDER BY amount;
SELECT * FROM orders LIMIT 3 ORDER BY amount DESC;
questions.ex: ORDER BY amount DESC sorts largest first and LIMIT 3 keeps the top three; LIMIT must come after ORDER BY.

questions.q: trades(trade_id, cpty_id) is joined to counterparties(cpty_id, name) with an INNER JOIN on cpty_id. Which rows are returned?
opts: All trades, with NULL names where no counterparty matches
All counterparties, even those with no trades
Every combination of trades and counterparties
Only trades whose cpty_id has a matching row in counterparties
questions.ex: An INNER JOIN keeps only rows where the join condition matches in both tables; unmatched rows require a LEFT or RIGHT JOIN.

questions.q: At which level of the SAP vendor master is the reconciliation account maintained?
opts: Company code level
General data (client level)
Purchasing organisation level
Plant level
questions.ex: The reconciliation account, along with payment terms and payment methods for accounting, sits in the company code segment because it links the subledger to a company code's general ledger.

questions.q: What is the correct order of steps in the SAP automatic payment program (F110)?
opts: Payment run → proposal run → maintain parameters → print payment media
Print payment media → maintain parameters → payment run → proposal run
Proposal run → print payment media → maintain parameters → payment run
Maintain parameters → proposal run (review and edit) → payment run → print payment media
questions.ex: Parameters define the run, the proposal lists items to pay for review, the payment run posts the payment documents, and payment media are then created.
